title: Fill the input sheets
guide-section: Working with a case
bread-crumbs: false
---

An economist does not type seventy fields by hand. You start from the shipped template snapshot and replace the cells you would have edited in yellow on Input 1–8.

```{python}
import inspect

import pandas as pd

from lic_dsf_2025_08_12 import api

print(inspect.signature(api.compute_external_dsa_risk_rating_signal))
len(api.ExternalDsaRiskRatingSignalInputs.describe())
```

The function takes one argument, `inputs`, whose type is `ExternalDsaRiskRatingSignalInputs`. That bundle has **77** leaves; the overall rating needs 89. Each name is the snake_case form of an Input-sheet series (plus a small engine leaf some rating functions also read). Unknown override names fail closed.

`from_workbook(path)` binds the same leaves from a populated workbook of this vintage, then accepts the same overrides.

## Discover fields with `describe()`

You do not need to guess field names, allowed values, or source cells. Every `*Inputs` bundle has a `describe()` class method. It returns a dictionary from field name to an `InputField` with four things on it: the allowed values (`Literal` choices or `Annotated` bounds, or a plain type when the workbook list is checked at construction), the axes and keys of a series, the template default, and the worksheet cell behind each value. Call it before you write any overrides:

```{python}
fields = api.ExternalDsaRiskRatingSignalInputs.describe()

names = [
    "country",
    "discount_rate",
    "external_domestic_debt_definition",
    "input6_tailored_tests_enabled",
    "input4_interest_rate",
    "input3_input_3_macro_gross_domestic_product_us_dollars",
]
pd.DataFrame(
    [
        [
            name,
            fields[name].values,
            ", ".join(axis.name for axis in fields[name].axes) or "scalar",
            fields[name].default if not fields[name].is_series else f"{fields[name].size} values",
            next(iter(fields[name].cells.values())),
        ]
        for name in names
    ],
    columns=["Field", "Allowed values", "Axes", "Default", "First cell"],
).style.hide(axis="index")
```

Drop the name filter to see all 77 fields. For a single field, read the attributes directly:

```{python}
tailored = fields["input6_tailored_tests_enabled"]
print("allowed values:", tailored.values)
print("default:", tailored.default)
print("cell:", tailored.cells[()])
```

`values` is the type annotation of one value. A `Literal[...]` lists the only choices the model accepts; an `Annotated` bound (for example a closed interval) is the numeric range. On this vintage many fields show a plain type (`str`, `float | str`) instead — those closed lists and intervals are still enforced when the bundle is built. Scalar fields have one cell, keyed by the empty coordinate `()`.

For a series, `axes` gives the axis names and their keys, and `cells` maps each coordinate to its worksheet cell. This is how you find the cell to edit in Excel for one creditor or one year:

```{python}
rates = fields["input4_interest_rate"]
gdp = fields["input3_input_3_macro_gross_domestic_product_us_dollars"]
pd.DataFrame(
    [
        ["input4_interest_rate", "INSTRUMENT", rates.axes[0].keys[:4], rates.cells[("IMF",)]],
        [
            "input3_input_3_macro_gross_domestic_product_us_dollars",
            "TIME_PERIOD",
            gdp.axes[0].keys[:4],
            gdp.cells[(2024,)],
        ],
    ],
    columns=["Field", "Axis", "First keys", "Cell for IMF / 2024"],
).style.hide(axis="index")
```

Each bundle describes only the fields its function reads. To find out whether an assumption affects a given output, check whether its name is in that bundle's `describe()`.

An out-of-domain value fails at construction, before any formula runs. A discount rate of `5` (percent, instead of the decimal `0.05`) and a tailored-test switch that is not `On` or `Off` are both rejected:

```{python}
try:
    api.ExternalDsaRiskRatingSignalInputs.from_defaults(discount_rate=5)
except ValueError as error:
    str(error)
```

```{python}
try:
    api.ExternalDsaRiskRatingSignalInputs.from_defaults(
        input6_tailored_tests_enabled="Maybe"
    )
except ValueError as error:
    str(error)
```

## Scalars you change first

These are the Input 1 / Input 2 / Input 6 switches that usually move first in a new vintage. The snapshot values come from the same `describe()` catalog:

```{python}
pd.DataFrame(
    [
        [name, fields[name].default, next(iter(fields[name].cells.values()))]
        for name in [
            "country",
            "first_projection_year",
            "discount_rate",
            "external_domestic_debt_definition",
            "input_1_rer_overvaluation",
            "input6_tailored_tests_enabled",
            "contingent_liability_soe_debt_pct_gdp",
            "contingent_liability_financial_market_pct_gdp",
            "ppp_capital_stock_shock_pct",
        ]
    ],
    columns=["Field", "Snapshot", "Cell"],
).style.hide(axis="index")
```

| Workbook cell | Field | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input 1 `C7` | `country` | LIC-DSF country names as spelled in the template (`Gambia, The`, `Congo, DR`, …) |
| Input 1 `C18` | `first_projection_year` | Integer year |
| Input 1 `C25` | `discount_rate` | Decimal in `[0, 1]` — `0.05` is 5 percent, not `5` |
| Input 1 `C31` | `input_1_rer_overvaluation` | Percent overvaluation |
| Input 1 `C33` | `external_domestic_debt_definition` | `Residency-based` or `Currency-based` |
| Input 6 `C6` | `input6_tailored_tests_enabled` | `On` or `Off` |

## Macro and financing series

Input 3–5 are labeled `Series` objects — immutable tensors with named axes, not plain lists. Build them from the described field's `default` so the axes and cell provenance stay attached. Nominal GDP on Input 3 is a single `TIME_PERIOD` axis covering history and the projection:

```{python}
gdp = fields["input3_input_3_macro_gross_domestic_product_us_dollars"].default
print("axes:", [axis.name for axis in gdp.domain.axes])
print("years:", gdp.domain.axes[0].keys[0], "…", gdp.domain.axes[0].keys[-1])
print("2024 GDP:", gdp.sel(TIME_PERIOD=2024))
```

`sel` drops the axes you fix. For a one-axis series that is just the observation. You can also index with the year itself (`gdp[2024]`) or the coordinate tuple (`gdp[(2024,)]`).

Input 4 interest rates are keyed by `INSTRUMENT` — the same creditor rows as the external-financing sheet:

```{python}
rates = fields["input4_interest_rate"].default
pd.DataFrame(
    [
        [instrument, rates.sel(INSTRUMENT=instrument)]
        for instrument in ("IMF", "Eurobond", "PPG ST external debt")
    ],
    columns=["Instrument", "Interest rate"],
).style.hide(axis="index")
```

Exports of goods and services (Input 3) use the same year axis as GDP:

```{python}
exports = fields["input3_input_3_macro_exports_of_goods_and_services"].default
exports.sel(TIME_PERIOD=2024)
```

On the snapshot, 2024 nominal GDP is about **45.5 billion** US dollars and exports of goods and services are about **18.7 billion**. IMF credit is priced at 0.25 percent; the Eurobond and short-term PPG external rows are 9 and 10 percent.

## Override one cell, keep the rest

Pass keyword overrides into `from_defaults`. The call below is the Excel action “type 4 percent in Input 1 `C25`”:

```{python}
api.compute_external_dsa_risk_rating_signal(
    api.ExternalDsaRiskRatingSignalInputs.from_defaults(discount_rate=0.04)
)
```

The mechanical external rating stays **High**. A one-point cut in the discount rate is not enough to move this snapshot off the High bin.

To edit a time series, rebuild it from the described field's `default` with `with_records` (or `with_values` when you already have a complete list in axis order). Both keep the schema and cell provenance. The example raises 2024 nominal GDP and leaves every other year untouched:

```{python}
gdp = fields["input3_input_3_macro_gross_domestic_product_us_dollars"].default
gdp_revised = gdp.with_records(
    (coord, 50_000.0 if coord == (2024,) else value)
    for coord, value in gdp.items()
)
pd.DataFrame(
    [
        ["2024 template", gdp.sel(TIME_PERIOD=2024)],
        ["2024 revised", gdp_revised.sel(TIME_PERIOD=2024)],
        ["2025 unchanged", gdp_revised.sel(TIME_PERIOD=2025)],
    ],
    columns=["Year", "Nominal GDP"],
).style.hide(axis="index")
```

Pass `gdp_revised` as `input3_input_3_macro_gross_domestic_product_us_dollars` in `from_defaults`.

`with_values` is the same idea when you already have a complete list in axis order. The Eurobond row on Input 4 is 9 percent in the snapshot; the call below rebuilds the whole `INSTRUMENT` series at 7 percent for that creditor and leaves every other rate — and the Input 4 cells — attached:

```{python}
rates = fields["input4_interest_rate"].default
instruments = rates.domain.axes[0].keys
rates_revised = rates.with_values(
    [0.07 if instrument == "Eurobond" else rates[instrument] for instrument in instruments]
)
pd.DataFrame(
    [
        ["Eurobond template", rates.sel(INSTRUMENT="Eurobond")],
        ["Eurobond revised", rates_revised.sel(INSTRUMENT="Eurobond")],
        ["IMF unchanged", rates_revised.sel(INSTRUMENT="IMF")],
    ],
    columns=["Instrument", "Interest rate"],
).style.hide(axis="index")
```

Two-axis series (Input 4 disbursements are `INSTRUMENT` × `TIME_PERIOD`; customized public deltas are `INDICATOR` × `TIME_PERIOD`) use the same pattern: iterate `items()`, change the coordinates you care about, and call `with_records`.

## Sheet → field groups

| Workbook sheet | Typical fields |
| --- | --- |
| Input 1 – Basics | `country`, `first_projection_year`, `discount_rate`, `external_domestic_debt_definition`, `input_1_rer_overvaluation` |
| Input 2 – Debt coverage | `contingent_liability_*_pct_gdp`, `ppp_capital_stock_shock_pct` |
| Input 3 – Macro-debt | `input3_input_3_macro_*`, `input3_input_3_external_debt_*`, `input3_domestic_*`, `input3_old_debt_service`, `input3_new_disbursements` |
| Input 4 – External financing | `input4_interest_rate`, `input4_grace_period`, `input4_loan_maturity`, `input4_disbursements`, `input4_blend_variant` |
| Input 5 – Local-debt financing | `input5_grace_period`, `input5_interest_rate_on_domestic_debt`, `input5_maturity`, `input5_gfn_share` |
| Input 6 – Tailored / standard tests | `input6_tailored_tests_enabled`, `input6_commodity_group_relevant`, `input6_standard_*` (including the optional B1–B3 shock sizes on `Input 6(optional)-Standard Test`) |
| Input 8 – SDR | `input8_sdr_stock`, `input8_sdr_interest_rate` |
| Customized scenario – public | `customized_public_include_scenario`, `customized_public_delta`, overflow and initial-stock scalars |

::: {.callout-tip}
Keep one `from_defaults(...)` call in your notebook. Change one keyword, re-run the rating functions, and you have a one-assumption sensitivity — the same discipline as shocking a single yellow cell and pressing F9.
:::
